data_quality_findings: 427 records from 2026.10.02_12.16.18 to 2026.10.02_12.47.53 (1895 s); all timestamps parse and none goes backwards; 74 records share a second with the previous record and gaps reach 93 s, so sampling is not uniform.
The header has 270 named columns; data rows carry 91-151 fields (fewer than the header, never more); all 90 core fields are aligned in every row; no exact duplicate rows.
No Level = -201 loss-of-coverage code and no out-of-range value in any Table II field; Level and Qual are numeric in all 427 records.
NR SS-SINR is '-' in 7 of 221 records labelled 5G (valid N 214); NR SS-RSRP and SS-RSRQ are populated in all 221.

LTE pool = 206 values from 4G-labelled records + 220 anchor values from 5G-labelled records = 426; 1 5G-labelled record has empty SecondCell fields; 1 4G-labelled record has SecondCell values populated (not used).

In all 7 5G-labelled records with missing NR SINR, Level and Qual equal LTE values (6 equal the record's own LTE anchor, 1 equals the next 4G record) and each is immediately followed by a 4G record; they are kept in NR RSRP/RSRQ; excluding them moves the NR RSRP mean from -99.07 to -99.44 dBm.

12 of the 25 4G-labelled records directly preceding a 5G record carry Level and Qual identical to that 5G record's NR values (all 12 differ from the LTE anchor RSRP reported next); they are kept in the LTE pool; excluding them moves the LTE RSRP mean from -92.85 to -92.75 dBm.
Readings are sample-and-hold: the Level/Qual/SNR triplet equals the previous record's in 38.9% of 5G-labelled and 32.5% of 4G-labelled records, so records are not independent samples.

LTE SNR in 4G-labelled records is never below 0 dB (min 0.0; 31 of 206 values exactly 0.0) while the LTE anchor SNR in 5G-labelled records is negative in 57 of 220; all 57 poor LTE SINR samples come from anchor values, so a floor at 0 dB in 4G-labelled records cannot be excluded and the LTE SINR poor share may be understated.
In 5G-labelled records Node, CellID, PSC, ARFCN and BAND equal the LTE anchor fields in 220 of 221 records; no NR ARFCN, NR PCI or NR band is logged; CSI_* and NRSTATE are empty in all records.
Operatorname is 'orange' in all records, but the serving-cell operator code is 22610 in 224 and 22601 in 203 records; each of the 18 nodes maps to exactly one code.
No active test was run: Test_Status, PING* and TESTDOWNLINK/TESTUPLINK are empty in all 427 records, so throughput and RTT are N/A; DL_bitrate/UL_bitrate are passive traffic (max 1458 / 326 kbps).

GPS: all 427 fixes are numeric and in range, accuracy 1-23 m; 63 records lie on frozen positions that end in a jump (6 jumps: distance/(gap+1 s) > 80 km/h with logged Speed <= 10 km/h) and are excluded from spatial outputs only (valid for spatial use: 364).
FOREGROUND first turns false at 2026.10.02_12.20.49; 59.5% of the records fall in the first 14.3% of the time (271 s), so sample shares over-represent the start of the drive.
The events file (79 rows) is identical to the main-log EVENT/EVENTDETAILS columns apart from the LOG START marker; 3 events have the same node and cell on both sides (only ARFCN or PCI differs).
LTERSSI is not above RSRP in 135 of 206 4G-labelled records (median difference 0 dB), so it does not behave as a wideband RSSI and is not used; 11 records deviate by more than 15 dB from that median.
CQI is '-' in 137 records and equals 6 in 73; TA is 0 or empty in all records; neither is used.

Timestamps are handset local time with no time-zone field; BANDWIDTH lists carriers without band labels (a 100 MHz entry appears in 142 5G-labelled and 88 4G-labelled records), so the NR band cannot be resolved.

anomaly_candidates.what: Observation: the 4G/5G label flips 50 times, every time on an unchanged node and cell, and 5G->4G changes mostly follow a non-poor NR sample. Hypothesis: the NR leg is added and released with traffic demand or inactivity; the fallback alone is not evidence of a coverage failure.
anomaly_candidates.evidence: NetworkTech flips: 25 4G->5G, 25 5G->4G (50 on same Node+CellID); last valid NR sample before a 5G->4G change: SS-RSRP >= -110 dBm in 20 of 25 (median -98.0 dBm), RSRP >= -110 and SINR >= 0 in 18; first 4G record in State I in 24 of 25; State D share 50.2% of 5G-labelled vs 21.8% of 4G-labelled records

anomaly_candidates.what: Observation: mixed-RAT values next to a label change. Hypothesis: Level/Qual, SNR and the RAT label are refreshed asynchronously (stale readings); such values bias the NR and LTE pools slightly.
anomaly_candidates.evidence: 7 5G-labelled records with SNR "-" whose Level/Qual equal LTE values; 12 4G-labelled records whose Level/Qual equal the NR values of the next 5G record; example: 2026.10.02_12.16.20 4G record Level -70 dBm, 2026.10.02_12.16.21 4G record Level -96 dBm, next 5G record NR Level -96 dBm with LTE anchor -68 dBm

anomaly_candidates.what: Observation: position frozen with Speed 0 and FOREGROUND=false, then a jump. Hypothesis: location updates stalled while the application was in the background, so position and Speed are stale and "stationary" cannot be assumed.

Observation: frequent cell changes with immediate returns to the previous cell, many between cells of the two operator codes; whether the handset was moving cannot be verified for most of them (stale GPS). Hypothesis: overlapping cells or layers of similar level; no root cause is asserted.
anomaly_candidates.evidence: 79 events in 1895 s (2.50 per minute): 61 reselection-type, 18 handover-type; 28 immediate A->B, B->A reversals (18 within 10 s, 26 within 30 s); 36 events change operator code, 18 change ARFCN, 33 stay on the same node; 52 logged with Speed 0, 60 with FOREGROUND=false, 50 on stale-position records

anomaly_candidates.what: Observation: events whose source and target are the same node and cell (only ARFCN or PCI differs), each directly after an event into that cell. Hypothesis: one cell change logged as two events because identity fields update one after another; the event total may be inflated by these.

Observation: IRAT-type events are not RAT changes of the record label, and "5G" event types refer to LTE anchor cells; the types describe LTE (anchor) cell changes plus the label state, not NR cell changes.
anomaly_candidates.evidence: 17 of 18 IRAT-type events lie between two records with the same NetworkTech label; only 1 event coincides with one of the 50 label flips; the source RAT in EventType differs from the previous record label in 17 events; identity fields equal the LTE anchor fields in 220 of 221 5G-labelled records

anomaly_candidates.what: Observation: LTE RSRP (Level) and LTERSSI disagree by more than 15 dB from their usual difference in the same record. Hypothesis: one of the two values is stale or belongs to the other RAT (not refreshed after a cell or label change).

anomaly_candidates.what: Observation (aligned inter-KPI relationships): SINR and RSRQ rise with RSRP on both layers and NR level follows the LTE anchor level; passive DL bitrate shows no relation with NR level. Coefficients are descriptive only (held, unevenly spaced samples); passive bitrate depends on traffic demand and is not a capacity or throughput measurement.
anomaly_candidates.evidence: Spearman: NR RSRP-SINR 0.724 (n=214), NR RSRQ-SINR 0.940, LTE RSRP-SINR 0.516 (n=426), NR RSRP vs anchor LTE RSRP 0.611 (n=220; NR minus LTE median -6.0 dB), NR RSRP vs passive DL kbps in State D -0.030 (n=111); NR RSRP poor in 31 records, of which SINR < 0 dB in 15
